advisories.reason: monaco-editor 0.57.0 (latest) runs its own vendored DOMPurify 3.4.15, so an npm override would only silence the audit, not change the shipped code. Exploitation requires sanitize(node, { IN_PLACE: true }); Monaco's domSanitize.js only sanitizes strings (RETURN_DOM_FRAGMENT / RETURN_TRUSTED_TYPE) and the app never imports DOMPurify. Remove when Monaco ships DOMPurify >= 3.4.17.
Same vendored DOMPurify 3.4.15 in monaco-editor 0.57.0; this advisory also requires IN_PLACE mode on a Node input, which Monaco never uses. Remove when Monaco ships DOMPurify >= 3.4.17.

Same vendored DOMPurify 3.4.15 in monaco-editor 0.57.0 (latest); an npm override would not change the shipped code. Remove when Monaco ships DOMPurify >= 3.4.17.
